result.title: LLM knowledge for improved Out-of-Distribution Tabular Prediction - A Cross-Validated Regularisation Approach
result.summary: Prediction models degrade when the deployment population differs from the one used to train them, and training data cannot say which feature-response relationships will transfer. Expert elicitation is slow and unscalable. We ask whether coefficient priors elicited from large language models (LLMs) improve out-of-distribution (OOD) prediction as the shrinkage target of a regularised regression instead of zero, across five tabular datasets split on real covariates, selecting providers and prior structures by source-domain cross-validation alone. The priors help on four of five datasets, by up to 7.9% OOD mean squared error, and ten of twenty-four prior-informed results resolve the mean improvement at conventional confidence; single-deployment intervals are much wider. On classification the gain is in probabilistic accuracy, not ranking, and control tests with corrupted priors attribute the benefit to feature-specific content rather than scale. Two findings temper this. Variation across candidate priors exceeds the average benefit, yet cross-validation margins fall below their own noise, so selection avoids the worst prior rather than finding the best. On three datasets the prior improves in-domain accuracy as much as out-of-domain, making it better regularisation than shift correction. Only where the training data are large enough that the in-domain gain disappears does elicited knowledge demonstrably improve transfer. Code, priors and results: https://github.com/hugohammer/llm-priors-ood.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出用 LLM 引出的系数先验代替零作为正则化收缩目标，在五个按真实协变量划分的表格数据集上，仅凭源域交叉验证选择模型提供方与先验结构，检验其能否改善 OOD 预测，并报告收益主要来自特征特定内容而非先验尺度。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「以 LLM 先验充当收缩目标、并以交叉验证在候选先验间做选择」的做法，可能可供核查如何把外部先验注入 latent 推理状态或监督目标，以及候选方案间选择裕度低于噪声的评估问题；与视觉/多模态推理无直接联系。
